title: Corporate Systems Policy Kit and Operational Playbooks
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document provides a single, practical kit of company-wide policies and operational playbooks for corporate systems and services. It consolidates access and permissions controls, change management procedures, data lifecycle rules, procurement and expense flows, vendor due-diligence steps, travel allowances, and ready-to-use internal templates. The goal is consistent decision-making, auditable approvals, and a fast path for repeatable operations.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and approved third-party vendors who request access to corporate systems or execute company transactions.
- Excludes product model-serving endpoints and customer-managed private deployments (see eng-private-deployments reference pages).

Key Contacts and Ownership

- Policy owner: Finance & Legal (owner_team).
- Operational stewards: IT Operations (day-to-day access), Security (controls & audits), Procurement (vendor & purchasing), People Ops (travel & expenses).
- Escalation path: policy-owner -> Head of Finance -> General Counsel -> CEO for high-risk exceptions.

1) Access and Permissions

Principles

- Least privilege by default.
- Role-based assignment and time-bounded approvals for sensitive systems.
- All privileged grants require a ticket with approval chain.

Classifications and Roles

- Role: employee-basic — access to corporate email, SSO portal, and internal wiki.
- Role: dev-ops — additional access for CI/CD, non-production infra. Requires manager + platform owner approval.
- Role: infra-admin — full production administrative rights. Requires manager + Security + 2FA on hardware token and annual reapproval.

Access Request Workflow (step-by-step)

1. Open an access request in the IT ticketing queue (queue: IT-ACCESS). Include business justification, requested role, and duration.
2. Manager review (24 hours target).
3. Service owner approval (48 hours target).
4. Security reviews any infra-admin requests (72 hours target).
5. Access provisioned with start/end timestamps; auto-expire on end date.

Temporary Elevated Access (breakglass)

- Breakglass is for emergency remediation only. Requester opens an incident-linked ticket; duty manager issues a time-limited token (max 4 hours) and notifies Security. Post-incident, requester files a normal access request and documents justification.

Access Audit Controls

- Quarterly audit of all infra-admin accounts.
- Monthly orphaned-access report: accounts unused for 90+ days flagged for deprovisioning.
- Audit evidence: ticket IDs, approver names, start/end times, and PAM logs.

2) Change Management (Corporate Systems)

Change Types and Approval Matrix

- Standard Change: pre-authorized, low risk (e.g., scheduled patch for a corporate app). Requires change owner and notification only.
- Normal Change: requires technical reviewer + manager + change manager approval.
- Emergency Change: implementation prior to formal approval allowed only with post-implementation review.

Change Submission Checklist

- Change ID, owner, business justification, components affected, rollback plan, test plan, planned window, and backout contacts.

Example change template (YAML snippet)

---
change_id: CHANGE-2027-045
owner: "eng-infra@example.com"
affected_services: ["vpn", "okta-sso"]
planned_window: "2027-03-15T02:00:00Z/2027-03-15T03:00:00Z"
rollback_plan: "Revert routing table and redeploy previous config from tag v1.4.2"
---

Change Review Timelines and SLOs

- Normal change review complete within 3 business days.
- Emergency change notification within 2 hours, formal documentation within 48 hours post-implementation.

Testing and Rollback Requirements

- All normal changes must include a test plan and a documented rollback step that restores state within a 30-minute RTO for critical services.

3) Data Management and Classification

Classification Labels

- PUBLIC — information intended for public consumption.
- INTERNAL — non-sensitive internal information.
- CONFIDENTIAL — contains business-sensitive material (financials, legal).
- RESTRICTED — regulated or customer-sensitive data (PII, customer secrets). Default retention, encryption, and access restrictions scale by class.

Retention and Deletion Rules

- Internal communications: retain 2 years.
- CONFIDENTIAL: retain 7 years unless otherwise specified.
- RESTRICTED: retention per contract; default 7 years and delete on contract end plus 90 days.

Encryption & Key Management

- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are managed through the corporate KMS. HSM-backed keys required for regulated workloads.

Data Handling Procedures (examples)

- Transferring RESTRICTED files: use approved SFTP or encrypted artifact store; email attachments with RESTRICTED content are forbidden.
- Analytics workbench: de-identified copies only unless explicit contract terms permit identifiable data and reviewers sign off.

4) Procurement and Expenses

Procurement Thresholds and Approvals

- Under $2,500: team lead approval.
- $2,500–$25,000: department head + Procurement review.
- $25,001–$150,000: VP-level + Procurement + Legal review.
- >$150,000: Executive sign-off and Board notification for capital commitments over 3 years.

Purchase Process (step-by-step)

1. Initiate a purchase request in the procurement system (Form: PR-NEW). Include business case and estimated TCO.
2. Procurement validates vendor, budget, and contract templates.
3. Legal conducts contract review for agreements >= $25,001 or any agreement storing RESTRICTED data.
4. Finance finalizes purchase order and records budget codes.

Expense Reimbursement Rules

- Use the corporate expense tool. Receipts required for any item > $25. Cardholder must submit within 30 days. Noncompliant claims will be denied.
- Per diem: domestic $85/day, international regional bands (See travel section).

Allowed Card Usage and Controls

- Corporate cards issued to managers with monthly limits. Card use for subscription SaaS requires an approved purchase request. Cards are audited quarterly.

5) Vendor Management and Due Diligence

Vendor Tiers and Requirements

- Tier 1 (High Risk — handles RESTRICTED data or critical infrastructure): Security questionnaire + SOC2 or equivalent + annual penetration test + contract with SLA and indemnities.
- Tier 2 (Medium Risk): Security questionnaire + annual attestation.
- Tier 3 (Low Risk): Basic vendor intake form.

Vendor Intake Checklist

- Business justification, estimated spend, data classification, country of operation, sanctions screening result, insurance certificates, and assigned vendor owner.

Contract Clauses (required for Tier 1/2)

- Data processing addendum, breach notification timelines (<=72 hours), right to audit, subprocessor list, and termination assistance.

Vendor Offboarding

- Exit checklist: revoke access, certify data return/destruction, collect final invoices, and update asset register. Evidence stored in procurement ticket.

6) Travel Policy (Corporate Travel for Conferences and Customer Meetings)

Booking and Approvals

- All travel requires a travel request submitted in the travel portal. For travel with spend > $3,000, department head approval required in advance.

Per Diem and Lodging

- Lodging: reasonable rate up to the company cap by city band. Use corporate booking portal for negotiated rates.
- Meals and incidental: domestic per diem $85/day; international per diem based on destination band (A/B/C).

Travel Safety and International Travel

- For international travel to Level 3 advisories, formal business justification and 1:1 security review required. Traveler must enroll in the company travel safety program.

7) Internal Templates and Forms (Quick Start)

Provided templates (copy & adapt):

- Access Request Template (to paste in IT ticket):
    Title: Access request: <system> — <role>
    Fields: requester, manager, start_date, end_date, justification, approvers

- Change Request Template (YAML snippet in change system): included earlier in the change section.

- Vendor Intake Form: vendor_name, contact, tier, country, data_classification, estimated_annual_spend, insurance

- Expense Reimbursement Template: date, merchant, business_purpose, amount, currency, receipt_id

8) Auditing, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

- Quarterly policy reviews by Finance & Legal and Security.
- Annual tabletop exercise covering breakglass and vendor breach scenario.
- KPIs to monitor: average access request lead time (goal <=48h), percent of changes with complete rollback plans (goal >=98%), vendor onboarding time (goal <=10 business days).

Exception and Risk Acceptance Process

- Exceptions must be requested via the policy-exceptions workflow and include compensating controls. Approval requires policy owner sign-off and a documented expiry for the exception (max 12 months).

Appendices

A. Approval Matrix (summary table)

| Action | Approver(s) | Threshold | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Access (infra-admin) | Manager + Security | n/a | 2FA required |
| Purchase | Procurement + Legal | >$25k | Attach contract |
| Travel (high-cost) | Dept Head | >$3k | Pre-approve |

B. Vendor Due Diligence Quick Checklist

- Sanctions check: OK
- Insurance: Certificate on file
- Security posture: SOC2 or questionnaire reviewed
- Contract: DPA + breach notification

C. Sample CLI for revoking access (example)

# revoke access for a user with ticket ID
redwood-cli access revoke --ticket IT-ACCESS-1234 --user alice@example.com --reason "role change"

D. Evidence and Artifact Storage

- Primary evidence stored in the ticketing system. Contracts in the corporate contracts repository (legal-concord). Sensitive evidence pointers recorded in Vault audit logs.
